title: Hello Robot awarded $3 million to develop Stretch robot for elder care
key_facts: Hello Robot received a Phase IIB SBIR grant from the National Institute on Aging (NIH), nearly $3 million over three years
Aim: use its Stretch mobile manipulator robot to support older adults with mild cognitive impairment and early Alzheimer's
Partner: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; project began 22 Sep 2026 and runs to May 2029
Three areas: cognitive assistance, social engagement and safety management
Study includes 60 older adults, care partners and staff, and an eight-week evaluation in care settings
quote_evidence: Hello Robot has received a Phase IIB Small Business Innovation Research grant from the National Institute on Aging, part of the National Institutes of Health.
The three-year Phase IIB project began on September 22, 2026, and is expected to continue through May 2029.
why_it_matters_hint: A US government research grant funds testing a home-care robot with people who have early dementia.
event_date: grant project began 22 Sep 2026; reported 4 Oct 2026
notes: Based on a project announcement with company quotes; the grant start of 22 Sep is earlier than the report but the announcement is new.
